note: Documented cases found by web search on 22 October 2026. Each claim is what the cited source reports. Where sources disagree, the case says so. A record may cite a case from this pool only; any other claim must be written as an inference from the model's principle.

cases.case: Cuba's free medical training and doctors per head
cases.claim: Cuba had one medical school in 1959 and 24 by 2012 to 2013, and it trains doctors without tuition fees. The Latin American School of Medicine takes roughly 1,500 students a year and had graduated more than 10,000 by 2013. Its free tuition attracts foreign students, including 23 Americans who were avoiding debt of 150,000 to 200,000 US dollars from a US medical degree. A Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives fact sheet ranks Cuba first in the world for doctors per head.
cases.source: Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives, Fast facts on revolutionary health care (secondary); Vassar College blog on Cuba's commitment to international healthcare (2012); Kaieteur News (2013)
cases.caveat: The per-head figures disagree: a 2012 opinion piece gives about 67 doctors per 10,000 residents, and a 2012 Vassar-hosted blog gives almost 6 per 1,000. The two do not reconcile. The school's founding year is given as 1998 by one source and 1999 by others.

cases.case: The Royal College of Physicians, from Henry VIII's charter of 1518
cases.claim: Henry VIII's charter of 1518 founded the Royal College of Physicians, formally on 23 September 1518. Six prominent physicians, Linacre among them, lobbied for the college. The charter let the six founders license qualified practitioners and bring prosecutions against malpractice, with an initial remit of the City of London and a seven-mile radius. An Act of Parliament in 1523 widened the college's reach across England.
cases.source: Royal College of Physicians, history of the college (history.rcp.ac.uk); The History Press, 500 years of the Royal College of Physicians (secondary)
cases.caveat: Sources disagree on whether Parliament passed the charter in 1518 or only confirmed it in 1523. The college's full name postdates the charter and was given statutory standing by Parliament in 1960.

cases.case: Specialty training places in the NHS, 2024 to 2026
cases.claim: Applications for NHS specialty training rose by 39.5 per cent in 2024 to about 59,700, for 12,743 posts, which is about 4.7 applicants per post against 1.9 in 2019. The British Medical Association warned that up to 20,000 doctors could be shut out of their chosen specialty in 2025. A mid-2025 BMA survey found that 52 per cent of second-year foundation respondents had no confirmed August post. The government announced 1,000 extra specialty places over three years, with priority for UK graduates, which the Royal College of Anaesthetists considers a small fraction of what is needed.
cases.source: The Doctor (BMA), Specialty training squeeze (2025); BMA, Urgent call to expand training places; Workplace Journal, Half of resident doctors face joblessness as training bottlenecks deepen (July 2025)
cases.caveat: The 52 per cent is a survey share, and the 20,000 is a projection, not an official count. The new places were due to accept applications from April 2026, and the search found no 2026 reporting on their effect.
